source_text:
Εὐχαριστίας καὶ πρυσευχῆς ἀπέχονται, διὰ τὸ μὴ ὁμολογεῖν τὴν εὐχαριστίαν σάρκα εἶναι τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τὴν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν παθοῦσαν, ἣν τῇ χρηστότητι ὁ πατὴρ ἤγειρεν. οἱ οὖν ἀντιλέγοντες τῇ δωρεᾷ τοῦ θεοῦ συζητοῦντες ἀποθνήσκουσιν: συνέφερεν δε αὐτοῖς ἀγαπᾶν, ἵνα καὶ ἀναστῶσιν.
πρέπον ἐστὶν ἀπέχεσθαι τῶν τοιούτων καὶ μήτε κατ’ ἰδίαν περὶ αὐτῶν λαλεῖν μήτε κοινῇ, προσέχειν δὲ τοῖς προφήταις, ἐξαιρέτως δὲ τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ, ἐν ᾧ τὸ πάθος ἡμῖν δεδήλωται καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασις τετελείωται. τοὺς δὲ μερισμοὺς φεύγετε ὡς ἀρχὴν κακῶν.
thought_title: Abstain from those who deny the Eucharist
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Smyrnaeans against teachers who deny the real flesh of Christ, and now he turns to their practice of staying away from the Eucharist and prayer.
pass_a_gloss: From Eucharist and prayer they abstain, because of the not confessing the Eucharist to be flesh of the Savior of us Jesus Christ, the [flesh] for the sins of us having suffered, which by the kindness the Father raised. The ones therefore speaking against the gift of God, disputing, die; it was better however for them to love, in order that also they might rise. Fitting it is to abstain from such [people] and neither privately about them to speak nor publicly, but to attend to the prophets, especially however to the gospel, in which the passion to us has been revealed and the resurrection has been perfected. The divisions however flee as beginning of evils.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for the communal meal of bread and cup
Fixed glossary term for the real flesh of Christ
Keeps the aorist participle's completed action tied to the flesh
Fixed glossary term for division in the church
Literal rendering of the phrase; 'evils' keeps the plural force

pass_b_english: They abstain from the Eucharist and from prayer, because they do not confess that the Eucharist is the flesh of our Savior Jesus Christ, the flesh that suffered for our sins and that the Father raised up in his goodness. So those who speak against the gift of God die in their disputing. It would have been better for them to love, so that they might also rise.

It is fitting to abstain from such people and not to speak about them either privately or publicly, but to attend to the prophets and especially to the gospel, in which the passion has been made clear to us and the resurrection has been brought to completion. Flee divisions as the beginning of evils.
notes: πρυσευχῆς is a misspelling of προσευχῆς in the source; glossed as 'prayer'.

last_rejected.quote: it would have been better for them to love
last_rejected.why: συνέφερεν is past tense ('it was better'/'it would have been better'), but the Greek gnomic aorist expresses a timeless truth; English conditional weakens the force.
last_rejected.fix: it was better for them to love
last_rejected.ruling: συνέφερεν is imperfect/aorist idiom; 'it would have been better' is standard rendering, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: τῇ χρηστότητι refers to God's kindness/mercy, but more precisely in context it is the Father's raising power; however 'goodness' is within semantic range.
last_rejected.ruling: χρηστότης means goodness/kindness; 'goodness' is within normal range, not a mistranslation.

last_rejected.quote: and not to speak about them either privately or publicly
last_rejected.source_quote: μήτε κατ’ ἰδίαν περὶ αὐτῶν λαλεῖν μήτε κοινῇ
last_rejected.why: English omits περὶ αὐτῶν ('about them'), making the prohibition seem like general silence rather than specifically not speaking about these people.
last_rejected.fix: and not to speak about them either privately or publicly
last_rejected.ruling: 'about them' is implied by context and 'such people' above; not a meaning-changing omission.

polish.changed: Clarified the antecedent of 'they' as the opponents Ignatius warns against, smoothed the sentence rhythm, and made the turn from the opponents' fate to the church's proper response more natural for reading aloud.

notes.why: Eucharist and love-feast may be distinct or same; reader cannot tell.
notes.fix: Note whether 'love-feast' is the agape meal distinct from Eucharist.
